payload.headline: 7-day activation dropped materially, concentrated in calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces (query_id q_16014efb9035)

cause.does_not_prove: Concentration in one segment does not by itself identify the mechanism or specific cause of the drop within that segment.
cause.text: Overall activation_rate_7d fell from 0.4011 to 0.3717 (-7.33% relative, p=5e-6) between baseline (2026-01-05 to 2026-02-08) and recent (2026-02-09 to 2026-03-01) periods, and the drop is concentrated in calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces, which fell from 0.3937 to 0.3061 (-22.25% relative, p=0.0), while calendar_provider=google (-0.42%, p=0.838747) and calendar_provider=none (+8.29%, p=0.281091) did not move significantly.

cause.does_not_prove: Timing alone does not prove this release caused the microsoft-segment activation drop; it only establishes the change as a candidate cause aligned with the onset.

evidence.quote: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

cause.text: Release rel_0412 ('Onboarding v2: connect calendar first') shipped 2026-02-10, one day after the recent period's onset, forcing new users to connect their calendar before anything else and removing the previous skip option.

cause.does_not_prove: A funnel correlation does not prove the specific blocking reason inside the connect step; ticket evidence is needed for that.
cause.text: For calendar_provider=microsoft, calendar_connect_rate_1d rose from 0.3321 to 0.5315 (+60.04%, p=0.0), but first_meeting_rate_7d fell from 0.5248 to 0.4469 (-14.84%, p=0.0) -- the earliest funnel step moving in the same negative direction as activation_rate_7d (-22.25%, p=0.0) -- indicating the forced calendar-connect step gets more people to connect but fewer go on to record a first meeting.

cause.does_not_prove: This search matched 8 distinct accounts total, but one of the 8 uses calendar_provider=google with the same template wording, so the count is not purely microsoft-specific; ticket volume is also small relative to the scale of the metric drop and does not show how many affected workspaces churned silently without filing a ticket.

evidence.quote: I just signed up and the setup won't let me past connecting Outlook. It says I need admin approval. Is there a way to skip this for now?
Is there a way to record a meeting without connecting my calendar? The Outlook step keeps failing with a permissions message.

cause.text: Support tickets from Microsoft-calendar workspaces opened after rel_0412 describe getting blocked by an admin-approval/permissions error when connecting Outlook, with no way to skip and proceed to a first meeting: "I just signed up and the setup won't let me past connecting Outlook. It says I need admin approval. Is there a way to skip this for now?" and "Is there a way to record a meeting without connecting my calendar? The Outlook step keeps failing with a permissions message."

payload.cheapest_test: Restore the skip option (or bypass the forced calendar-connect step) for calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces only, via a flag scoped to calendar_provider, and compare first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d for new Microsoft signups over the next 1-2 weeks against the current forced-connect flow.
payload.question: Did 7-day activation change in the last few weeks, and why?
payload.recommendation: Roll back rel_0412's forced calendar-connect-first step (no skip) for calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces, since the entire material activation loss is concentrated there and traces to users getting blocked by an Outlook admin-approval/permissions error with no way to proceed to a first meeting.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: Does not fully rule out that channel or company_size contribute independently, only that neither dimension offers a clean isolated segment the way calendar_provider does.
ruled_out.text: Channel and company_size do not isolate the change the way calendar_provider does: every channel segment moved in roughly the same -7% to -8% direction (direct -7.19% p=0.042351, organic -7.48% p=0.007141, paid_search -8.17% p=0.063043, recap_link -7.71% p=0.004398) and most company_size segments moved similarly (s11_50 -6.64% p=0.050056, s2_10 -7.28% p=0.002179, s51_plus -15.46% p=0.006693, solo -5.96% p=0.063996), whereas among calendar providers only microsoft moved materially while google (-0.42%, p=0.838747) and none (+8.29%, p=0.281091) stayed flat.

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Whether the Outlook admin-approval block is a genuine Microsoft 365 tenant/IT policy requirement (unavoidable) or a Tallybird-side OAuth scope bug (fixable)
Total silent drop-off volume beyond the 8 tickets found in q_b8f0be047b80
Whether flags.yaml already has a lever to scope rel_0412's connect-first/no-skip behavior by calendar_provider (flag_state lookup was denied this session)
would_change_if: If a broader ticket/account-level check showed the Outlook admin-approval block affects only a small fraction of the -14.84% first_meeting_rate_7d decline (most of the drop having another cause), rollback would be premature.

If next week's data shows first_meeting_rate_7d for microsoft recovering without any code change, this would suggest a transient issue rather than one caused by rel_0412, favoring no_action/monitoring over rollback.

payload.hypothesis: Restoring the skip for Microsoft calendar workspaces brings their activation back to baseline.
payload.kill_trigger: Microsoft first_meeting_rate_7d not back to its week 1 to 5 level for cohorts after the rollback

findings.claim: bld_0001 implements a rollback of rel_0412's forced calendar-connect-first step scoped to calendar_provider=microsoft only (matching act_0001's params), leaving google/none workspaces on the current connect-first flow.
findings.evidence: act_0001 specifies segment.calendar_provider=["microsoft"]; the build's location name ('rollback-rel-0412-microsoft-skip') suggests matching scope, but flag_state (the tool that would confirm the actual flag rule and its match keys) was denied to this reviewer this session -- the same gap the source decision packet pkt_0001 itself listed as an open unknown before the build was made ('Whether flags.yaml already has a lever to scope rel_0412's connect-first/no-skip behavior by calendar_provider ... flag_state lookup was denied this session'). review.check only validated fields/privacy and returned numbers/quotes as n/a; it does not confirm scope.
findings.impact: pkt_0001's own evidence shows google (-0.42%, p=0.84) and none (+8.29%, p=0.28) workspaces were unaffected or improved by the connect-first flow. If the flag rule is not actually keyed to calendar_provider=microsoft and instead reverts the connect-first behavior globally, this would regress the two segments that were not broken, undoing an otherwise-working change for the majority of workspaces.
findings.proof_required: Mechanism proof: a flag definition or config snippet showing the match condition is calendar_provider=microsoft, not a global toggle.
findings.smallest_action: Attach the flags.yaml diff or a flag_state read showing the new rule's match key is calendar_provider=microsoft (and defaults to enabled:false per policy) to this build entry before it reaches the PM.
